quest.title: To the Lighthouse
quest.description: Your explorative footsteps echo on the island. There is no one around, and the sole lighthouse remains silent in the darkness...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.speaker: Panicking Phantom
dialogues.text: The lighthouse... It's lit! The Wild Hunt! The Wild Hunt is attacking! To arms!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gloomy skies over here... The air's all icky and sticky and dark and damp.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Remember how Flins said that he lives in a graveyard to the north? Is this, uh, really the place...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's not a person in sight. Just a tower, and.... Oh!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Flins?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Ah, good day, you two — assuming I don't have the time wrong.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Phew! Well, it's nice to see a living person here. Hiya, Flins. So this is where you live, huh?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Yes, this is my humble home, the tomb of the Lightkeepers.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Did an adventurer's curiosity bring you here to this lonely isle? I am at pains to imagine any other cause.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're not wrong. We haven't explored this area yet.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: As guardian of the tombs here in the Final Night Cemetery, allow me to extend the warmest of welcomes to you both, on behalf of the spirits who slumber here eternally.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, do you mean there really are ghosts here?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: That is correct. As you may have noticed, this island is dotted with headstones. You might think of it as a veritable necropolis filled with souls — isn't it a welcoming thought?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not at all! If anything, this place just got scarier!

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Ah, apologies. It was meant merely as a gesture of the hospitality that you deserve as guests. We don't receive many visitors here, after all.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: But I suppose it is a tall order to expect people to suppress their fear of ghosts... Even so, I do hope your visit shall be a pleasant one.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: The spirits on this isle, while somewhat old-fashioned and hardly gregarious, are an unassuming crowd who keep to themselves. I have found they make perfectly decent neighbors.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: If you still have misgivings, I can only suggest that you avoid staying outside where possible. The ghosts do not tend to set foot indoors very often.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Although, that might render your sightseeing experience a little less riveting... Let me think...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Most of the camps on this isle have been removed, and only the lighthouse remains, symbolizing the many battles the Lightkeepers have fought against the Wild Hunt. In that regard, it has quite a bit of historical value, and is thus well worth seeing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that was the first thing we saw when we arrived. So it's a lighthouse, huh? What happened to the light?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Years of disrepair and a shortage of fuel, I'm afraid. As this island became abandoned, maintaining the lighthouse became increasingly difficult. Besides, even if we were to rally sufficient manpower to repair it, it would serve little purpose these days.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: In the past, it guided people on their way to and from the island... but all those people now lie beneath our feet in eternal rest.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: ...Well, that is perhaps not entirely accurate. They do sometimes come running out, speaking once-familiar utterances into the void.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: In which case, since you are not used to the darkness that shrouds this island, you could consider restoring the lighthouse to illuminate your way.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: I, too, know well the comfort that a distant ray of light can bring on those lone journeys through the cold night.

choices.text: Do you not need the lighthouse, Flins?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Speaking as a Lightkeeper, we no longer need the building all that much, and I am under no official obligation to maintain it.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: And personally, I am more partial to the night than the day, so I find myself quite comfortable here in the dark.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Besides, I have a lantern of my own. I would rather tend to that than rely on a more distant warmth.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: As such, you should have no issues using it, so long as it helps you.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: I believe there should still be some backup fuel for the lighthouse stored in an old tent to the north. That should be enough to serve your present needs.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Gotcha.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: And if you should need to find me, I will be in an underground basement on the north side. That's where I will be sorting through my reports.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: I will meet up with you once I have completed my urgent tasks.

choices.text: Are we really allowed to operate a Lightkeeper lighthouse?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Well, it is an important testament to our history, but as is the case with many once-magnificent buildings from the past, it now lies desolate and neglected.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Not that the Lightkeepers have forgotten about it, of course. We are simply spread too thinly.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: But you will merely be lighting it up, not vandalizing it. Rest assured, you will face no objections.

choices.text: Could you help us with that?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Alas, if only I could — I would enjoy nothing more than the pleasure of your company. Today, however, is when the post from headquarters arrives.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: I already have many reports to write, and with a new round of correspondence incoming, I fear I can afford to delay responding to the previous batch no longer.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: So please excuse me while I complete some of my paperwork. I shall accompany you as soon as I am able.

choices.text: Will lighting the lighthouse be a difficult task?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: In general, the upkeep is quite an undertaking. It requires regular reporting to Piramida, which is quite a distance away, and transport of fuel back and forth. The tower and the light themselves also need to be cleaned and maintained.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: But to simply light it up, you need only add some fuel and activate the lamp.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: It has merely been in a state of disuse, not disrepair.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: It is always dark in the "Final Night Cemetery," so I simply made a guess, presuming that you'd prefer to act during the day. It seems I was mistaken.

choices.text: Honestly, I don't know what time it is either.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Then let us forgo these niceties. It is always dark here in the Final Night Cemetery — time becomes somewhat meaningless.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Either way, let's try not to get their attention. Let's just grab the fuel and go!

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: The sky is so dark. I'm scared. They're staring at me...

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: You sure took your time, didn't you? C'mon, help me shift this fuel. It's almost time for our lighthouse shift.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: D—Does he mean...

response.speaker: Wandering Phantom
response.text: Heh, look at you, shaking like a leaf. You scaredy-cat. How you made the cut as a Ratnik, I'll never know.

response.speaker: Wandering Phantom
response.text: C'mon, grab your stuff and let's go. Perhaps I'll even tell you a ghost story on the way. Haha!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? A ghost telling us ghost stories... Wait, hang on, was he just trying to scare us?

response.speaker: Wandering Phantom
response.text: You ever heard of the "blue fire"?

response.speaker: Wandering Phantom
response.text: As we all know, when you're out walking out at night, you should never look behind you, and never look all the way down at the ground. Always look ahead, into the distant skies.

response.speaker: Wandering Phantom
response.text: Well, that's because the Wild Hunt watches us from the darkness. They wait for you to lose your way in the fog, and then, when you're at your most vulnerable, they come and take your life.

response.speaker: Wandering Phantom
response.text: That's why it's dangerous to travel alone in the dead of night. But sometimes, if you're lucky, you'll see a blue lantern shining out in the darkness...

response.speaker: Wandering Phantom
response.text: They say it only appears if you run in to the Wild Hunt, or if you can't find your way at night. Either way, if you ever see the blue lantern appear, you must remember to follow it.

response.speaker: Wandering Phantom
response.text: Don't ask me what it is, 'cause I don't know. My granddad says it's one of the fae that used to live in Nod-Krai in ancient times, but it could equally be the ghost of one of our fallen warriors, one who truly hated the Wild Hunt...

response.speaker: Wandering Phantom
response.text: Whatever it is, the blue lantern seems to be on our side — the side of the Lightkeepers. I'll bet that's why the Starshyna wants to make offerings to it on the island, haha.

choices.text: Ignore him. Let's just keep moving.

talks.objective: Ascend the lighthouse to light the tower up

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Finally, we're here! Let's find where the fuel goes and pour it in.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Paimon finds the fuel slot and pours in the fuel. Then, you ignite the lamp at the top of the lighthouse.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woohoo, the light's on! This should make things way easier. Now we can keep exploring!

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: To the lighthouse! To the lighthouse, ███! We've gotta get a signal to the units outside before they reach us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's still going on about the signal... Did we send the wrong one? Let's try another.

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: Great, the light's on! Guess I won't have to worry about moving fuel anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, it's the ghost from before who was talking about moving fuel. What's he doing over here?

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: The Wild Hunt came... It passed through all the graves!

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: The fog clung to our ears, stuck to our mouths... We couldn't see or hear each other...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What's he talking about? Has the Wild Hunt really showed up? Paimon didn't see it at all.

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: To the lighthouse! To the lighthouse, ███! We've gotta get a signal to the units outside before they reach us!

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: Don't just stand there gaping, ███! Pull yourself together! Every second we hesitate could mean another dead comrade!

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: Have you forgotten how to send signals!? Come on, I've told you before, a Lightkeeper always has to be prepared!

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: We're all gonna die... they'll strip the bones from our spines...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Something's off — all the ghosts are coming this way...

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: We too shall cry tears of blood...

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: The Wild Hunt is here, we've got to think of something quick! Um... Okay, we'll try and stall them at the base of the lighthouse while you head up to the top!

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Phantom
dialogues.text: Up to the top... signal... think of something...

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: If you've forgotten how to send signals, check the handbook. We nailed it to the tower for moments just like this.

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Phantom
dialogues.text: Do not fear ███, do not fear ███...

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: Don't leave our bodies to the Wild Hunt, I beg of you! That is no way to die!

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Phantom
dialogues.text: Death... Wild Hunt... go to the lighthouse...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The ghosts have surrounded the tower... Should we do what they're asking?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like they need us to head up, find the handbook, and use the lamp to send a signal out.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Phantom
dialogues.text: Lighthouse... hope... everlasting night...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The handbook says that we've gotta aim the lamp in the right direction, then control the brightness according to the signaling rules.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are five signal types: Distress, warning, guidance, summoning, and all safe. The part that describes the warning signal is illegible, so let's try one of the others.

dialogues.speaker: Desperate Phantom
dialogues.text: It's too late... There's no point calling for help now.

dialogues.speaker: Desperate Phantom
dialogues.text: Even if reinforcements from Piramida do arrive from the north, they'll only end up as fodder for the Wild Hunt, just like us...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: The north it is, then.

talks.objective: Operate the lighthouse according to the handbook's instructions

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: In need of my help so soon? One moment, let me sort these letters out.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: What happened here? Ran into a spot of bother?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: A whole host of ghosts surrounded the lighthouse. I sent them away to prevent them from blocking the area...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: And when they saw the lighthouse flashing, they departed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It was pretty scary... They completely surrounded us and begged us to help them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It was a little unexpected.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I sensed it too. This graveyard is bereft of life save for passing birds, the insects underground, and myself. Normally, it's so quiet you can hear yourself breathing.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Up until just now, that is, when these ghosts started getting agitated... Was it because of the lighthouse?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Flins what happened before and after you lit the lighthouse up...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: They asked you to send a signal out? Hmm... How peculiar. In my experience, they have never coerced or harmed anyone in any way.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: This can only mean that lighting the lighthouse has somehow caused a change in them. I must say, this is quite out of the ordinary.

choices.text: Did you see anything else unusual on the way here?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: The ghosts here tend to stick to fixed areas and repeat words and phrases that meant something to them in life. But now, all eyes are on the lighthouse.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: They have a rather indistinct appearance, but when they fix their yearning strongly on a specific place, I can sense where their cold attention is directed.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Consider it a... natural talent of mine. As to the cause of this behavior, I do have a theory.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What got into them, I wonder?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Ghosts are the echoes of living souls — a portion of their thoughts and memories that, for certain reasons, fails to enter the Ley Lines at the moment of their death. And thus they linger on the surface.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: The ghosts in question were Lightkeepers in life and as such, I believe the lighthouse is deeply embedded in their memories — something they are instinctually drawn to.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Re-lighting it must have stirred something in their memories, causing them to depart from their usual behavior.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: You might not be aware of this lighthouse's past, but it once served a great many functions, from guiding passing merchants and Lightkeeper fleets to reporting on the Wild Hunt's activity in the surrounding area.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: In the days before this was a graveyard, its light was never once extinguished.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: It came to symbolize the hope and warmth that the Lightkeepers sought to bring to Nod-Krai.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: But alas, the light of this historic outpost was snuffed out in a conflict against the Wild Hunt several decades ago.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: According to our internal records, that conflict cost the island ninety percent of the troops stationed here. The Starshyna of that time eventually decided to send a warning signal to the outside.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, a warning signal? So they didn't use a distress signal and call for help?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Indeed. The warning signal saved the nearby merchant fleets and patrolling Lightkeeper ships. Without it, they likely would have been pulled into the fighting with little knowledge of the situation.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: But at the same time, this signal also cut the troops on the island off from any possibility of rescue.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: The Lightkeeper oath contains a line that goes as such:

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: "Our bones and blood we shall use as fuel, we shall make life greater than death."

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: It is a line that strikes at the very heart of our principles. Should we find ourselves at a great disadvantage, we are to prioritize the preservation of life and ensure humanity's long-term survival.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: After all, the Wild Hunt is a never-ending threat, while our numbers are limited. This principle is most cruel to those who must sacrifice themselves, and yet most of us willingly abide by it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Shoot... So we sent out a distress signal, but what the ghosts actually wanted was for us to send a warning signal, right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Whoops...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: You feel you unwittingly did something wrong? No, I don't think so.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Ghosts are but the memories of people that once were. You may have stirred up those memories, but that is all they are — those to whom they once belonged are long gone.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Still, I can see that you're concerned about them, and truthfully, so am I. If you wish to find them... just follow me.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Ah, yes — and please do not be alarmed by anything strange we may encounter along the way.

choices.text: Well, they've left now. Any idea where they went?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Unfortunately, although I saw them leaving, I did not get the chance to ask them where they were going.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: But you sent a distress signal out, yes? I suspect that may give us some clues.

dialogues.speaker: Trembling Phantom
dialogues.text: Look! Someone's put out a distress signal! Reinforcements will arrive from the sea soon! Hold steady, everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Hmm... The coast, then... But on which side?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon sees them! They're all gathering on the beach!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Had reinforcements arrived on the day of that battle, they would have landed here.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: You have to understand that ghosts are hard to reason with. A better way to communicate is to give them key information that might provoke some sort of a reaction.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: How about this? We'll go in together, but I'll handle the communication. After all, I'm not only a Lightkeeper myself, but also very accustomed to dealing with ghosts.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like a plan.

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: Don't come near us... Don't try to save us.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Help is on the way.

dialogues.speaker: Grieving Phantom
dialogues.text: The Wild Hunt is coming in too fast, there's no time. Let us stay here and take them down with us.

dialogues.speaker: Solemn Phantom
dialogues.text: This place will be enough of a graveyard by the time the night is through... Don't send more people to their deaths...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: So, you don't need rescuing?

dialogues.speaker: Solemn Phantom
dialogues.text: No, we do! Please, save us... We can't hold on much longer...

dialogues.speaker: Grieving Phantom
dialogues.text: Everyone else is gone, and we are lost. What more can we do? Please, someone, anyone, save us.

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: ...Ignite the blue lantern. It will guide you far from the Wild Hunt...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: The blue lantern cannot bring back souls from the dead. Even if you light him up, it will be too late.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: He can help you destroy what remains of the Wild Hunt, but he cannot save you.

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: Don't rescue us. Don't come any closer... No, wait, help us, please! Someone, anyone...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's this supposed to mean? Do they want help, or don't they?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Those poor souls... On the one hand, they hoped that someone would send out a distress signal and save their lives. On the other, they did not wish to call in reinforcements only to send them to their deaths.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: And so they sought the help of the blue lantern spoken of in local legend, and indeed, one such lantern was still preserved on this island.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: That ought to have been their last hope in a time of desperate need. But to my great regret, it is of no use to them now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Will any other horrible things happen?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: They will recall the unfathomable suffering they experienced in their final moments. I will do what I can to comfort them...

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: "We shall part the snow-curtain of the sky, and blast the winter winds across the wasteland."

dialogues.speaker: Grieving Phantom
dialogues.text: We have sworn an oath, and so we must fight to the end.

dialogues.speaker: Solemn Phantom
dialogues.text: We cannot wait for them to come. We are the last ones. Pick up your weapon, ███.

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: "We are the Lightkeepers, who shine the eternal light of hope into the endless snow-swept plains."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... Flins, it seems like these ghosts have rallied?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Again, they are but the replaying memories of once-living people. It is not the ghosts who have rallied... but the Lightkeepers who fought to the bitter end.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Viewing the world through human eyes is like looking into a kaleidoscope. It is so complex, and yet... so beautiful.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: The sorrow and reluctance in the face of death, the longing for a life of peace and stability... the surprising valor that wells up in the hour of despair.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: #If it were up to you, {NICKNAME}, would you wish to do something for them?

choices.text: I might perhaps lend them a helping hand.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Is that so? A response befitting an adventurer of your caliber.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Personally, I do feel inclined to do something for them. To help these shadows of the heroes that once were forget the death that will soon be upon them, and return to their slumber.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: In time, the memories and yearning of these ghosts will fade, and slowly return to the Ley Lines... but that time has not yet come.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: My dear Ratniki, I am Kyryll Chudomirovich Flins. Once upon a time, it was I who retrieved your fallen bodies from the battlefield.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Now, let me once more lay you to rest, for you are worthy of my respect and earnest esteem.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Look upon my flame, and wander no longer. Return to your graves and forever rest in peace.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Six feet under may you slumber in your erstwhile homeland, and in sweet dreams return to the Ley Lines' embrace.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They're... gone?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Some of their memories and thoughts have been dispersed. The rest will later return to their usual state.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: To me, they are both warriors whose memories should be honored, and my gentle, friendly "neighbors."

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Unfortunately, I did not know most of their names, but my short interaction with them has deposited some of their memories within my flame.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: At the very least, I know now that the gentleman who moved fuel and loved to tell the tale of the blue lantern was named "Aimo," and the comrade he always called out to was named "Eetu."

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Many of the ghosts on this island may have been affected by the lighthouse, and I'm not sure if they'll all undergo changes like Aimo.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: But if you're in the mood to keep exploring, would you come with me? I'd like to get to know them better still.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's do it.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: It would be my honor.

choices.text: May they soon return to the Ley Lines.
I might perhaps honor their destiny.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, the signal is sent! Let's go check on the ghosts.

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: To the lighthouse! To the lighthouse, ███! We've gotta get a signal to the units outside before they reach us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These ghosts seem really worked up... Should we just do what they're asking and see what happens?

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Phantom
dialogues.text: Let's go. "Our bones and blood we shall use as fuel..."

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Where are you going?

dialogues.speaker: Melancholic Phantom
dialogues.text: "We shall make life greater than death."

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Never mind. We won't get anything out of this one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gloomy skies overhead, just like the last time we were here... The air's all icky and sticky and dark and damp.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We didn't get a good look then. All Paimon remembers is that really tall tower. So let's explore the area more fully this time... Wait, is that...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, well it's good to see a familiar face. Especially in this darkness — it really gives you the heebie-jeebies...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: You needn't worry. This is my humble abode and the tomb of the Lightkeepers. And, while somewhat dark, it is on the whole a safe place.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: That being said, I rarely receive visitors here, save for the occasional colleague. What brings you two here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: To be honest, we just wanted to see where you live. We were in such a rush last time, we didn't get to do a proper tour.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I see. In that case, as guardian of the tombs here in the Final Night Cemetery, allow me to extend the warmest of welcomes to you both, on behalf of the spirits who slumber here eternally.

dialogues.speaker: Letter
dialogues.text: I have received your supply request, and HQ has approved it. I'll get Illuga to send it to you at the next opportunity.

dialogues.speaker: Letter
dialogues.text: P.S.: You sure you don't need some sort of pet, like a puppy or a kitten, to keep you company?

dialogues.speaker: Letter
dialogues.text: You haven't replied, so I've found you a dog.

dialogues.speaker: Letter
dialogues.text: If you still don't reply, Illuga's bringing the dog over to the "Final Night Cemetery," you hear?

dialogues.speaker: Letter
dialogues.text: Signed, Your Friend Nikita

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: To the lighthouse! To the lighthouse, ███! We've gotta get a signal to the units outside before they reach us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These ghosts seem really worked up... Should we just do what they're asking and see what happens?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There really are a ton of headstones here on this isle, and they're all so old you can't make out the words on 'em at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, this place is super dark. Feels kinda stuffy, too. Uh, and there are ghosts over there... B—But we'll be fine... right?

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: Ah, shucks, look at me talking away — I totally forgot, I've still got fuel to move!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, but we brought all the fuel with us! What's this guy talking about...

dialogues.speaker: Wandering Phantom
dialogues.text: Alright, I'd better get back. See you later, scaredy-cat! Hehe. It's nearly time for... my shift...
